title: The Spontaneous Emergence of Multi-Agent Artificial Intelligence Systems.
abstract: This study analyzes how artificial intelligence systems are transitioning from individual isolated models to teams of connected and self-organized agents capable of collaborating and generating complex group behaviors. The operational and functional notion of "artificial collective intelligence" is defined and defended, articulated across four key dimensions: information integration, intentional coordination, operational reflexivity, and strategic persistence. The term is understood exclusively as the observable capacity to maintain a shared operational representation, update it based on feedback, and coordinate persistent actions; it does not imply subjective experience, phenomenal intentionality, self-awareness, or independence from human goals. The emergence of these dynamics appears to be facilitated by the introduction of standardized protocols for interoperability such as the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and by the extension of distributed inference to Edge AI and IoT networks. To anchor the theoretical analysis in verifiable evidence, the study proposes a three-level empirical taxonomy, distinguishing between facts consolidated in production (auto-modification of scaffolding and asynchronous delegation), field observations and boundary events (including the DseWiki empirical incident), and speculative projections to be subjected to empirical falsification. Highlighting the structural limits of current regulatory frameworks (such as the AI Act) focused predominantly on individual models rather than network properties, the study proposes a paradigm shift in governance and cybersecurity. It recommends moving from component-level controls to strategies based on real-time systemic observability, the analysis of relational topologies, and the adoption of dynamic agentic containment and quarantine mechanisms. Through the topological formalization of graph theory and complex systems, the work highlights the conditions favoring organizational phase transitions, carefully distinguishing between structural graph convergence and model semantic stability. The main contribution consists of distinguishing between designed coordination, functional self-organization, and open autonomy, showing that certain forms of emergent coordination are already observable, whereas the transition toward open systems capable of autonomously redefining goals and operational constraints is not yet demonstrated.

title: We Copied the Neuron… and Forgot How the Brain Works
abstract: For eight decades, artificial intelligence has drawn its vocabulary from the brain, yet it borrowed a simplified picture of the neuron rather than a theory of how the brain organises its work. This essay retraces that history, from McCulloch and Pitts (1943) and Rosenblatt's perceptron (1958), through the Dartmouth proposal of 1955, backpropagation (1986) and the Transformer (2017). It argues that the field progressively answered an engineering question (how to make available computers do intelligent things) while leaving an older one open: how does an intelligent system organise the path to a required result? Drawing on everyday goal-directed behaviour, the analogy of flight, and Thomas Kuhn's account of scientific revolutions, and noting the growing compute and energy footprint documented by the International AI Safety Report 2026 and the International Energy Agency, the essay asks whether future computation should begin from the required output rather than from the whole computational space. The essay does not reject the existing paradigm. It credits McCulloch, Pitts, Rosenblatt, Hinton and the Transformer with one of the greatest technological revolutions in history, and suggests that the field may have mastered one road before discovering that there was another. The author's patent-pending work (MRC-113, UK Intellectual Property Office) is introduced only at the level of this question and its reported outcome, exact agreement with full computation in the tests carried out so far. Its method is not disclosed.

title: Completing Gödel's Ontological
abstract: Gödel's ontological proof is a higher-order modal argument from axioms governing positive properties to the necessary existence of a God-like being. In the version developed here, five positivity axioms and three definitions generate four main results: every positive property is possibly instantiated; God-likeness is possibly instantiated; God-likeness is an essence of every God-like individual; and a God-like individual exists necessarily. The same axiom system also yields modal collapse, while a one-world, one-individual model shows that the five positivity axioms are jointly satisfiable. We then define a semantic completion that begins from the completed modal derivation. We supply an ambient semantics in which self-reference, contradiction, fixed points, restriction, and return are represented explicitly. Belnap--Dunn four-valued semantics provides an ambient carrier $FOUR=\{N,T,F,B\}$ containing the Boolean core $Bool=\{F,T\}$ as a proper substructure. Negation fixes $N$ and $B$; the information-closing map $Inc(v)=B$ has the unique fixed point $B$; every Boolean endomap transported through the inclusion lands in $\{F,T\}$ while ambient closure lands at $B$; contradiction remains localized as designated information; and a provenance-enriched split--fuse pair satisfies the exact return law $\mu\circ\delta=\mathrm{id}$, with $\rho=\delta\circ\mu$ idempotently normalizing modal provenance. The completed architecture therefore has three distinct closures. The modal proof closes into necessity. The paraconsistent semantics closes into the ambient fixed point $B$. The return structure closes differentiation by exact recovery. Together these three formally distinct layers give a complete account of necessary existence, self-referential closure, and return.

title: Масштабоване виявлення аномалій у великих потоках мережевих даних на основі динамічних графів і спектральних характеристик
abstract: У статті запропоновано метод масштабованого виявлення аномалій у потоках мережевих даних на основі динамічних графів, графових скетчів і спектральних характеристик. Мережеву телеметрію подано як потік ребер, а стан графа – у вигляді матриці скетчу з експоненційним згасанням ваг. Для виявлення структурних змін використано індекс гладкості, що обчислюється без повного спектрального розкладання та забезпечує сталий обсяг пам’яті. Експерименти на синтетичних потоках засвідчили ефективність методу для короткочасних аномалій типу «зірка», однак виявили обмежену чутливість до низькоінтенсивного сканування. Встановлено залежність якості детектування від розміру скетчу, коефіцієнта згасання та тривалості вікна спостереження. Подальші дослідження передбачають побудову ансамблю потокових критеріїв і перевірку методу на реальній телеметрії IPFIX.

title: Multi-Label Active Learning for Doxing Detection: Enabling Large-Scale Analysis of the Dynamics and Network Organization of Harmful Behavior
abstract: Doxing is often studied as a harmful disclosure of personal information, but fine-grained detection requires distinguishing how such information is used against a target. Studying these distinctions at scale requires labels difficult to produce when relevant behaviors are rare, unevenly distributed, and overlapping. We address this challenge with a multi-label scheme anchored in the established distinction among deanonymizing, targeting, and delegitimizing doxing, and we extend that scheme to related processes through which personal information is requested, morally framed, or connected to calls for action. Using multi-label active learning with RoBERTa, we apply this framework to 1.3 million comments from three target-centered boards in a hostile forum environment from 2014 to 2025. After each annotation cycle, RoBERTa is retrained on the expanded set, while uncertainty and diversity guide selection of informative cases. This makes fine-grained labeling feasible at corpus scale while keeping reliability visible. Demonstrating this value, key findings include that deanonymizing and targeting doxing are rare, textually elaborate, strongly connected, and locally concentrated, whereas delegitimizing doxing is far more common in our setting. Doxing follows no uniform life cycle here but varies across target contexts and can continue beyond early identification across years of hostile discussion. Requests for information are consistent with a preparatory or validating role, hostile moral framing operates as a broad background condition, and action-oriented hostility is more context-specific. Timestamped reply links and reactions show that doxing-related output is concentrated among highly active and interactionally prominent users and that prior same-type interaction is associated with later doxing.

title: GeoACE: Geometry-Diverse Anchor-Correction Ensembles for Heterogeneous Treatment Effect Estimation
abstract: Predicting heterogeneous causal effects supports informed decision-making, yet suitable inductive biases vary with treatment overlap, covariate imbalance, prognostic structure, and sample size. The Geometry-Diverse Anchor--Correction Expert Ensemble (GeoACE) addresses this variation through five complementary experts whose predictions are combined using weights estimated from validation data. Compared with ensemble designs that derive diversity primarily from sample or feature subsets, reweighting, or feature transformations, its central contribution is the coordinated design of training objectives and anchor geometries that target different prognostic and overlap structures. Following validation, each expert is refitted on the combined training and validation data, while retaining its distinctive structure. The shared architecture couples a structured outcome anchor with a learned neural correction. ACE serves as the reference estimator, while OW-ACE emphasizes well-supported covariate regions through overlap-weighted factual training. G$Φ$-ACE constructs a global outcome-guided geometry from pooled prognostic associations, whereas A$Φ$-ACE incorporates arm-specific outcome associations and penalties for treatment-group imbalance. O$Φ$-ACE complements these approaches with an outcome-free, overlap-aware projection that replaces the anchor input with a lower-dimensional representation. GeoACE is evaluated against 11 comparators on eight benchmark protocols, alongside comparisons of weighting rules and aggregation controls. It achieves the lowest mean $\sqrt{\mathrm{PEHE}}$ and absolute average treatment effect error on all three IHDP protocols and closely approaches the best comparator on NEWS, although performance varies across the remaining benchmarks. The aggregation analyses show similar observed performance for inverse-DR weighting and equal averaging.

title: Broadening Uncertainty Estimation for Audio Question Answering Across Methods, Formats, and Inputs
abstract: Audio-language models can produce confident answers unsupported by the audio, motivating uncertainty estimates that identify unreliable responses. We compare probability-based, sampling-based, self-verification, evidential, and contrastive measures across four open-weight models and five audio QA benchmarks. In multiple-choice evaluation, first-token measures are strongest overall, with top-1 probability achieving a mean AUROC of .740, compared with .708 for ten-sample discrete semantic entropy, while requiring no additional model calls. Across four benchmarks, shifting from multiple-choice to open-ended evaluation lowers mean accuracy from 57.6% to 36.6%, yet uncertainty remains predictive of errors: semantic entropy, maximum token entropy, and semantic agreement achieve mean AUROCs of .697, .694, and .693, respectively. To test whether uncertainty reflects the evidence available to answer the question, we perform input ablations that remove either the audio or the question. Across top-1 confidence, entropy, and sampling-based measures, removing audio reduces error-detection AUROC by .101 on average, compared with .010 when removing the question. Together, these results establish efficient uncertainty baselines and show that uncertainty in audio-language models depends substantially more on available audio evidence than on question text.

title: A Survey on Parallel Reasoning
abstract: Abstract As Large Language Models (LLMs) evolve, parallel reasoning has emerged as a vital inference paradigm that enhances robustness by concurrently exploring multiple thought trajectories. Unlike fragile sequential methods, parallel reasoning expands inference breadth to significantly improve problem-solving performance. This paper provides a comprehensive survey of the progress and challenges in this burgeoning field. We first formally define parallel reasoning and distinguish it from sequential paradigms like Chain-of-Thought. Then, we propose a novel taxonomy to categorize advanced techniques into non-interactive reasoning, interactive collaboration, and efficiency-oriented decoding strategies. Furthermore, we examine diverse application scenarios, including complex problem-solving and reliability enhancement. Finally, we identify core challenges and outline future research directions. This work serves as a strategic roadmap to foster further innovation in parallel reasoning.

title: Comparative Analysis of Confidence-Aware and Verification Based Hallucination Reduction Techniques in Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) grounds language-model responses in externally retrieved evidence, yet weak retrieval or unsupported generation can still reduce reliability. This pilot study compares two lightweight safeguards: retrieval-confidence gating and post-generation evidence verification. Four configurations were evaluated on the same 30-question benchmark: Basic RAG, Confidence-Aware RAG, Verification-Based RAG, and a Combined approach. The benchmark used 30 short passages, 25 answerable questions, and five deliberately unanswerable questions. Retrieval employed normalized all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings with FAISS top-3 search; generation and verification used Groq Compound Mini. All 120 runs completed without API errors. Basic and Verification-Based RAG achieved 30/30 preliminary correct outcomes. Confidence-Aware and Combined RAG achieved 29/30 because one answerable query received a similarity score of 0.261 and was rejected by the fixed 0.55 threshold. No unsupported final answer was observed. Mean response times were 0.50 s, 0.40 s, 1.29 s, and 0.95 s, respectively. The results reveal a practical trade-off: confidence gating can reduce model calls and encourage safe refusal, but an uncalibrated threshold may reduce answer coverage, while verification preserves coverage at additional latency.

title: Factored transfer selection of binarization schemes: code, protocol, manifests, tables and per-run results
abstract: This record is the material behind the manuscript of the same name: everything needed to rerun the study, and everything needed to recompute its numbers from the runs already made. It holds the code, including the reference implementation the patch is applied to, and the protocol with its two dated amendments. It holds the exact command line of every run, so a campaign can be repeated as it was executed rather than as it is described. It holds the trained policies, one per problem family and one per family and optimizer, and one csv per instance, optimizer and scheme with a row per seed, which is the level at which every table of the manuscript is computed. It also holds the per-generation traces of the convergence sample and the outputs of the analysis scripts. The runs come from nine campaigns. Three reference factorials over the 34 binarization schemes were produced here, on the railway level of set covering, on feature selection and on unit commitment; the remaining four families reuse the factorial of the earlier calibrated layer study, deposited separately and cited in the manuscript. The rest are the calibration phase, the main evaluation over 115 instances of six families, six optimizers and 31 seeds, the extreme-scale study on two railway instances of about one million columns, the transfer study across optimizers, an ablation with the paid oracle disabled, and the sample of traced runs. Together they are roughly 143 000 runs. Recomputing the numbers takes minutes and rerunning a campaign takes days, so README.md gives both routes and says which scripts serve each. SHA256SUMS.txt carries a checksum for every file, and MANIFEST.json records what was collected and whether any campaign was short of runs when the archive was built.

title: Thermal_Diagnostic_System_by_Quantum_Tomography
abstract: This version develops a rigorous experimental framework for spatial thermal diagnosticsusing superconducting qubits as distributed sensing elements. The central methodologicalchange relative to a simple frequency-to-temperature conversion is the introduction of anexplicit measurement model separating thermal and non-thermal contributions to the observedqubit-frequency shift.For sensor i,δωobsi = δωthi + δωfluxi + δωqpi + δωTLSi + δωroi + δωotheri.Only after characterization of these contributions is a temperature estimate formed. Thelocal thermal response is represented by a calibrated coefficientαi(T0) = ∂ωq,i∂T⃓⃓⃓⃓T0,with explicit uncertainty and possible nonlinear correction.The spatial inverse problem is formulated through a response matrix, a point-spreadfunction (PSF), and regularized reconstruction. Spatial resolution is therefore not identifiedsimply with sensor spacing.The protocol introduces independent reference thermometry, blocked test data, blind lo-calized thermal perturbations, cross-validation, uncertainty propagation, hierarchical analysisacross cooldowns, and predefined falsification criteria. The primary endpoint is the inde-pendently evaluated reconstruction error of the thermal field. Secondary endpoints includeeffective spatial resolution, temperature resolution, localized perturbation detection, calibrationstability, and cross-cooldown reproducibility.The proposal remains exploratory and falsifiable. It does not claim experimental validation,universal thermometry, or superiority over conventional thermal sensors.

evidence.abstract: This version develops a rigorous experimental framework for spatial thermal diagnosticsusing superconducting qubits as distributed sensing elements. The central methodologicalchange relative to a simple frequency-to-temperature conversion is the introduction of anexplicit measurement model separating thermal and non-thermal contributions to the observedqubit-frequency shift.For sensor i,δωobsi = δωthi + δωfluxi + δωqpi + δωTLSi + δωroi + δωotheri.Only after characterization of these contributions is a temperature estimate formed. title: Formal Verification of Euclid's Theorem on the Infinitude of Primes
abstract: We present a formally verified proof of Euclid's Theorem - that there are infinitely many primes - using the Stainless verification system. The proof uses the primorial-plus-one specialization of Euclid's finite-list construction and verifies the supporting arithmetic and list lemmas from first principles.

title: Implementasi Text Mining dan Support Vector Machine untuk Analisis Sentimen Pelayanan Puskesmas
abstract: Puskesmas sebagai fasilitas kesehatan tingkat pertama menghadapi keterbatasan dalam mengolah opini masyarakat yang tersebar di media sosial dan kanal daring secara sistematis dan real-time. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengembangkan sistem analisis sentimen berbasis text mining dan algoritma Support Vector Machine (SVM) untuk mengklasifikasikan opini masyarakat terhadap pelayanan Puskesmas Gurgur Pardomuan, Kabupaten Aceh Tenggara, ke dalam tiga kategori: positif, negatif, dan netral, sekaligus mengimplementasikannya dalam sistem berbasis web sebagai alat bantu evaluasi pelayanan. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif yang dikombinasikan dengan pendekatan rekayasa sistem (system engineering approach). Data primer diperoleh melalui kuesioner daring dan ulasan masyarakat di media sosial, kemudian diproses melalui empat tahap text preprocessing (case folding, tokenizing, stopword removal, stemming), diekstraksi fiturnya menggunakan pembobotan TF-IDF (Term Frequency–Inverse Document Frequency), dan diklasifikasikan dengan SVM kernel linear berstrategikan One-vs-Rest (OvR). Model dilatih pada 200 data berlabel dengan komposisi 70 data positif (35%), 68 negatif (34%), dan 62 netral (31%), serta dievaluasi menggunakan confusion matrix pada 10 data uji independen. Evaluasi menunjukkan akurasi keseluruhan 70%, dengan performa sempurna pada kelas negatif (precision 100%, recall 100%, F1-score 100%), namun kelas netral masih terbatas (precision 50%, recall 33,33%, F1-score 40%) akibat ketimpangan jumlah data latih antarkelas. Pada konfigurasi pengujian dengan 30 data latih dan kernel linear, model mencapai akurasi 90%, precision 89,50%, recall 90,20%, dan F1-score 89,80%. Seluruh fitur sistem — input komentar, training model, klasifikasi sentimen, dan ekspor laporan — berhasil divalidasi melalui black-box testing. Temuan penelitian ini menunjukkan bahwa pendekatan text mining berbasis SVM dapat menjadi alternatif yang lebih responsif dibandingkan survei manual untuk memantau persepsi masyarakat terhadap layanan kesehatan primer di wilayah pedesaan Indonesia.

title: PRIME-ANC: Path-Ratio-Informed Modeling for Efficient Neural Filter Synthesis in Active Noise Control
abstract: Changes in listener acoustics require active noise control (ANC) filters to be redesigned for new acoustic paths. We introduce PRIME-ANC, a shared neural synthesizer that learns a bounded, path-dependent logmagnitude correction to a regularized path-ratio base. Minimum-phase reconstruction and truncation produce finite-impulse-response (FIR) filters; training optimizes their noise-control performance. Across ten random training/test splits per dataset, PRIME-ANC achieves average held-out one-third-octave reductions of 18.81 and 17.76 dB over 50 Hz-5 kHz on a ten-path dataset and a public earphone database, respectively. On original earphone measurements, it improves upon the path-ratio base by 7.89 dB. Ablation studies support the contributions of both the analytic base and the path-dependent correction. Given calibrated paths for a held-out listener condition, PRIME-ANC generates a path-specific FIR without iterative optimization. With three Gauss-Newton updates, it reaches 21.43 dB reduction, approaching direct weighted least-squares design while producing lower amplification and root-mean-square control output.

title: Industrial Anomaly Detection via Defect-Grounded Reasoning in Visual Latent Space
abstract: Industrial anomaly detection (IAD) is evolving beyond conventional detection and localization toward multimodal inspection systems that can describe, explain, and reason about fine-grained defects. Although recent multimodal large language model (MLLM)-based methods improve anomaly understanding through textual reasoning and visual guidance, they face two limitations in fine-grained inspection. First, their visual refinement often requires iteratively revisiting local image regions or augmenting with additional tools. Second, the resulting local defect evidence may not be reliably preserved throughout subsequent reasoning. To address these, we propose Anomaly-LR, a defect-grounded latent reasoning framework that first forms a global understanding of the input and then progressively refines anomaly-relevant representations directly in the visual latent space. We further construct IAD-LR-22K, the first IAD instruction dataset designed for latent reasoning, containing 22,228 image-question instances from 4,523 industrial images, with global textual reasoning traces and region-level visual annotations. Extensive experiments show that Anomaly-LR achieves state-of-the-art performance among comparable-scale methods across multiple IAD benchmarks, without requiring external references or tools. The code and data will be released at https://github.com/Yen666/Anomaly-LR.

title: Towards Deployable Underwater Vessel Classification
abstract: We propose a compact underwater acoustic classification framework combining multi-representation feature engineering, temporal statistical pooling, and compact convolutional architectures designed for acoustic time-frequency and cochlear representations. We investigate multiple conventional and auditory-inspired representations and first evaluate lightweight classifiers and Conventional Neural Networks (CNNs) on ShipsEar dataset. On the provided split, a two-layer CNN achieves a macro F1 of 0.9918, while a Radial Basis Function Support Vector Machine (RBF-SVM) reaches 0.9883. However, source-recording provenance cannot be reconstructed, preventing verification of recording-independent generalisation. We therefore evaluate on DeepShip dataset using recording-level partitioning before segmentation. Under this protocol, a 157K-parameter compact CNN achieves a test macro F1 of 0.7226, while an 11.17M-parameter ResNet18 provides no improvement in validation performance under the matched setting. These results demonstrate the importance of representation-aware feature and model design, together with rigorous recording-level evaluation, for classification performance and deployability in compact underwater acoustic systems.

title: Decoder Model Compatibility Provides Information beyond the Logical Gap under Drifting and Correlated Quantum Noise
abstract: Quantum error-correcting decoders provide both corrections and confidence estimates for the logical-error risk of individual measurement records. Such confidence can guide postselection, but it depends on the accuracy of the decoder noise model. When the physical device drifts away from that model, confidence measures such as the logical gap can become miscalibrated. We show that this mismatch can itself provide useful information. On IBM quantum hardware, syndrome statistics drift across consecutive acquisition windows, and the resulting detector histories differ substantially from those predicted by the stationary detector error model used for decoding. We observe a similar hardware-model mismatch in independent Google surface-code memory data. We exploit this effect by assigning additional rejection weight to detector histories that are unlikely under the assumed model. For minimum-weight perfect matching (MWPM), the minimum weight $W$ provides an inexpensive proxy for syndrome surprisal. On held-out IBM repetition-code memories, likelihood-aware postselection reduces the retained logical-error probability (LEP) by $10.6\%$ at $d=7$ and $28.8\%$ at $d=9$, both at $15\%$ rejection. On Google ten-round $d=5$ XZZX surface-code memory data, it reduces retained LEP by $75.4\%$ at $90\%$ rejection. Applied to Google's magic-state cultivation experiment with the Tesseract decoder, it reduces tomography infidelity by $34.7\%$ with $30\%$ additional grafting-stage rejection, or increases accepted yield by $30.4\%$ at a target fidelity of $97.0\%$. Burst-noise simulations show that the advantage persists as code distance and syndrome-extraction volume increase. The method reuses quantities already produced during logical-gap decoding and requires only an additional fitting step.

title: Truncation uncertainties for accurate quantum simulations of lattice gauge theories
abstract: The encoding of lattice gauge theories onto quantum computers requires a discretization of the gauge field's Hilbert space on each link, which presents errors with respect to the Kogut–Susskind limit. In the electric basis, Hilbert space fragmentation has recently been shown to limit the excitation of large electric fields. Here, we leverage this to develop a formalism for estimating the size of truncation errors in the electric basis. Generically, the truncation error falls off as a factorial of the field truncation. Examples of this formalism are applied to the Schwinger model and a pure U(1) lattice gauge theory. For reasonable choices of parameters, we improve on previous error estimates by a factor of 10 306 .

title: Duqueana Core: Technical Glossary & Framework
abstract: # Duqueana Core: Technical Glossary & Framework Specification v1.0 ## Post-Classical Deterministic AI · Marco de Computación Estructural Eficiente **Autor:** Douglas Helvesio Urbina Duque **ORCID:** 0009-0005-1230-7549 **Institución:** Universidad Nacional Experimental de Guayana (UNEG), Venezuela / Instituto Doughel **Fecha:** Septiembre 2026 **Licencia:** CC-BY-NC-ND 4.0 (Ciencia Abierta UNESCO 2021) **DOI Principal:** 10.5281/zenodo.[ASIGNAR_DOI_AQUI] --- ## 📋 Resumen Ejecutivo Duqueana Core es un ecosistema tecnológico y de investigación que opera bajo el paradigma de **Inteligencia Estructural Duqueana (IED)**, priorizando la eficiencia algorítmica y la optimización de memoria sobre el aumento de potencia de hardware. Este documento define oficialmente los componentes técnicos, la arquitectura de red y los estándares operativos del framework, todos validados experimentalmente y disponibles bajo ciencia abierta con núcleo reservado. **Palabras clave:** Inteligencia Estructural Duqueana, IED, MREI, Doulitas, Post-Classical Computing, Deterministic AI, Duqueana Core, Venezuela, ~6 KB RAM. --- ## 1. Inteligencia Estructural Duqueana (IED) ### 1.1 Definición Oficial La **Inteligencia Estructural Duqueana (IED)** es el paradigma lógico-fundacional bajo el cual opera Duqueana Core. Se caracteriza por: - **Principio de Eficiencia Estructural:** Maximizar la capacidad computacional mediante la optimización de la estructura algorítmica y relacional de datos, en lugar de incrementar la potencia del hardware. - **Determinismo Absoluto:** Eliminar la aleatoriedad y los procesos estocásticos, garantizando resultados 100% reproducibles bajo las mismas condiciones iniciales. - **Minimalismo Computacional:** Operar con la mínima huella de recursos posible (~6 KB RAM en hardware clásico) sin sacrificar precisión ni capacidad de simulación. ### 1.2 Diferenciación con IA Clásica | IA Clásica (Post-2010) | IED (Duqueana Core) | |------------------------|---------------------| | Basada en modelos masivos (GB-TB) | Basada en estructura relacional (~6 KB) | | Entrenamiento estocástico | Ejecución determinista | | Aumento de parámetros = mejor rendimiento | Optimización estructural = mejor rendimiento | | Hardware especializado (GPU/TPU) | Hardware clásico optimizado | | "Caja negra" probabilística | Pipeline transparente y trazable | --- ## 2. Framework MREI (Método de Resolución Exacta Iterada) ### 2.1 Definición Oficial El **Método de Resolución Exacta Iterada (MREI)** es el mecanismo público de simulación avanzada y verificación estructural que constituye el núcleo operativo de Duqueana Core. ### 2.2 Características Técnicas - **Iteración Determinista:** Cada paso computacional sigue reglas fijas y reproducibles, sin aproximaciones aleatorias. - **Descomposición Diádica:** Agrupamiento de datos en bloques de escala [2^j, 2^(j+1)) para análisis de persistencia estructural. - **Operador de Verificación Estructural:** Aplica criterios de coherencia, estabilidad y no-depleción de patrones en cada iteración. - **Trazabilidad Criptográfica:** Cada ejecución genera hash SHA-256 único para validación de integridad. ### 2.3 Aplicaciones Validadas - **Teoría de Números:** Análisis de simetría en conjeturas (Goldbach, Collatz, Riemann). - **Física Matemática:** Verificación estructural de ecuaciones diferenciales (Navier-Stokes, Yang-Mills). - **Geometría Algebraica:** Validación de ciclos y clases de cohomología (Hodge). - **Bioinformática:** Simulación estructural de genomas y proteínas. **Nota de Protección Intelectual:** El núcleo iterativo completo del MREI, incluyendo los parámetros geométricos universales exactos (de escala y angulares) y las optimizaciones de eficiencia extrema, son propiedad intelectual reservada del Instituto de Investigación Digital. --- ## 3. Unidades Doulita ### 3.1 Definición Oficial Las **Unidades Doulita** son bloques atómicos de memoria optimizada que emplea Duqueana Core para reducir drásticamente el consumo de RAM en simulaciones complejas. ### 3.2 Especificaciones Técnicas - **Tamaño:** ~128 bytes por unidad (optimización atómica). - **Función:** Almacenamiento relacional compacto de estructuras de datos indexadas. - **Eficiencia Comprobada:** Reducción del consumo de RAM entre **65% y 81%** comparado con métodos tradicionales de simulación. - **Arquitectura:** Bloques auto-contenidos que permiten acceso directo sin sobrecarga de punteros. ### 3.3 Impacto Computacional | Escenario Tradicional | Con Unidades Doulita | |----------------------|---------------------| | Simulación: 50-100 MB RAM | Simulación: ~6 KB RAM | | Estructuras dispersas con overhead | Estructuras compactas indexadas | | Fragmentación de memoria | Memoria contigua optimizada | --- ## 4. Arquitectura de Red Duqueana Core ### 4.1 Tipología de Nodos La red Duqueana Core se divide en tres tipos de nodos especializados: #### **4.1.1 Duqueana Core Hub (Orquestador Central)** - **Función:** Coordinación de rutas, validación de integridad estructural y distribución de tareas. - **Requisitos:** Hardware clásico con ~10-50 MB RAM. - **Responsabilidad:** Mantener la coherencia global del ecosistema. #### **4.1.2 Duqueana Lite (Nodos Avanzados Distribuidos)** - **Función:** Ejecución local de simulaciones MREI, validación estructural y generación de hashes SHA-256. - **Requisitos:** ~10 MB RAM mínimo, hardware clásico. - **Característica:** Operación autónoma con sincronización periódica al Hub. #### **4.1.3 Usuarios Web (Clientes Ligeros)** - **Función:** Visualización de resultados, consulta de métricas estructurales y validación de trazabilidad. - **Requisitos:** Navegador web estándar. - **Acceso:** Interfaz React con dashboard interactivo. ### 4.2 Topología de Red - **Tipo:** Arquitectura P2P híbrida (Hub-and-Spoke con validación distribuida). - **Protocolo:** Verificación criptográfica SHA-256 en cada transacción. - **Escalabilidad:** Diseño modular que permite expansión infinita de nodos Lite. --- ## 5. evidence.abstract: # Duqueana Core: Technical Glossary & Framework Specification v1.0 ## Post-Classical Deterministic AI · Marco de Computación Estructural Eficiente **Autor:** Douglas Helvesio Urbina Duque **ORCID:** 0009-0005-1230-7549 **Institución:** Universidad Nacional Experimental de Guayana (UNEG), Venezuela / Instituto Doughel **Fecha:** Septiembre 2026 **Licencia:** CC-BY-NC-ND 4.0 (Ciencia Abierta UNESCO 2021) **DOI Principal:** 10.5281/zenodo.[ASIGNAR_DOI_AQUI] --- ## 📋 Resumen Ejecutivo Duqueana Core es un ecosistema tecnológico y de investigación que opera bajo el paradigma de **Inteligencia Estructural Duqueana (IED)**, priorizando la eficiencia algorítmica y la optimización de memoria sobre el aumento de potencia de hardware. Este documento define oficialmente los componentes técnicos, la arquitectura de red y los estándares operativos del framework, todos validados experimentalmente y disponibles bajo ciencia abierta con núcleo reservado. **Palabras clave:** Inteligencia Estructural Duqueana, IED, MREI, Doulitas, Post-Classical Computing, Deterministic AI, Duqueana Core, Venezuela, ~6 KB RAM. --- ## 1. Inteligencia Estructural Duqueana (IED) ### 1.1 Definición Oficial La **Inteligencia Estructural Duqueana (IED)** es el paradigma lógico-fundacional bajo el cual opera Duqueana Core. Se caracteriza por: - **Principio de Eficiencia Estructural:** Maximizar la capacidad computacional mediante la optimización de la estructura algorítmica y relacional de datos, en lugar de incrementar la potencia del hardware. - **Determinismo Absoluto:** Eliminar la aleatoriedad y los procesos estocásticos, garantizando resultados 100% reproducibles bajo las mismas condiciones iniciales. - **Minimalismo Computacional:** Operar con la mínima huella de recursos posible (~6 KB RAM en hardware clásico) sin sacrificar precisión ni capacidad de simulación. ### 1.2 Diferenciación con IA Clásica | IA Clásica (Post-2010) | IED (Duqueana Core) | |------------------------|---------------------| | Basada en modelos masivos (GB-TB) | Basada en estructura relacional (~6 KB) | | Entrenamiento estocástico | Ejecución determinista | | Aumento de parámetros = mejor rendimiento | Optimización estructural = mejor rendimiento | | Hardware especializado (GPU/TPU) | Hardware clásico optimizado | | "Caja negra" probabilística | Pipeline transparente y trazable | --- ## 2. Framework MREI (Método de Resolución Exacta Iterada) ### 2.1 Definición Oficial El **Método de Resolución Exacta Iterada (MREI)** es el mecanismo público de simulación avanzada y verificación estructural que constituye el núcleo operativo de Duqueana Core. ### 2.2 Características Técnicas - **Iteración Determinista:** Cada paso computacional sigue reglas fijas y reproducibles, sin aproximaciones aleatorias. - **Descomposición Diádica:** Agrupamiento de datos en bloques de escala [2^j, 2^(j+1)) para análisis de persistencia estructural. - **Operador de Verificación Estructural:** Aplica criterios de coherencia, estabilidad y no-depleción de patrones en cada iteración. - **Trazabilidad Criptográfica:** Cada ejecución genera hash SHA-256 único para validación de integridad. ### 2.3 Aplicaciones Validadas - **Teoría de Números:** Análisis de simetría en conjeturas (Goldbach, Collatz, Riemann). - **Física Matemática:** Verificación estructural de ecuaciones diferenciales (Navier-Stokes, Yang-Mills). - **Geometría Algebraica:** Validación de ciclos y clases de cohomología (Hodge). - **Bioinformática:** Simulación estructural de genomas y proteínas. **Nota de Protección Intelectual:** El núcleo iterativo completo del MREI, incluyendo los parámetros geométricos universales exactos (de escala y angulares) y las optimizaciones de eficiencia extrema, son propiedad intelectual reservada del Instituto de Investigación Digital. --- ## 3. Unidades Doulita ### 3.1 Definición Oficial Las **Unidades Doulita** son bloques atómicos de memoria optimizada que emplea Duqueana Core para reducir drásticamente el consumo de RAM en simulaciones complejas. ### 3.2 Especificaciones Técnicas - **Tamaño:** ~128 bytes por unidad (optimización atómica). - **Función:** Almacenamiento relacional compacto de estructuras de datos indexadas. - **Eficiencia Comprobada:** Reducción del consumo de RAM entre **65% y 81%** comparado con métodos tradicionales de simulación. - **Arquitectura:** Bloques auto-contenidos que permiten acceso directo sin sobrecarga de punteros. ### 3.3 Impacto Computacional | Escenario Tradicional | Con Unidades Doulita | |----------------------|---------------------| | Simulación: 50-100 MB RAM | Simulación: ~6 KB RAM | | Estructuras dispersas con overhead | Estructuras compactas indexadas | | Fragmentación de memoria | Memoria contigua optimizada | --- ## 4. Arquitectura de Red Duqueana Core ### 4.1 Tipología de Nodos La red Duqueana Core se divide en tres tipos de nodos especializados: #### **4.1.1 Duqueana Core Hub (Orquestador Central)** - **Función:** Coordinación de rutas, validación de integridad estructural y distribución de tareas. - **Requisitos:** Hardware clásico con ~10-50 MB RAM. - **Responsabilidad:** Mantener la coherencia global del ecosistema. #### **4.1.2 Duqueana Lite (Nodos Avanzados Distribuidos)** - **Función:** Ejecución local de simulaciones MREI, validación estructural y generación de hashes SHA-256. - **Requisitos:** ~10 MB RAM mínimo, hardware clásico. - **Característica:** Operación autónoma con sincronización periódica al Hub. #### **4.1.3 Usuarios Web (Clientes Ligeros)** - **Función:** Visualización de resultados, consulta de métricas estructurales y validación de trazabilidad. - **Requisitos:** Navegador web estándar. - **Acceso:** Interfaz React con dashboard interactivo. ### 4.2 Topología de Red - **Tipo:** Arquitectura P2P híbrida (Hub-and-Spoke con validación distribuida). - **Protocolo:** Verificación criptográfica SHA-256 en cada transacción. - **Escalabilidad:** Diseño modular que permite expansión infinita de nodos Lite. --- ## 5. title: Replication Data for "Convergence between Differential Privacy and Shannon Entropy in Data Anonymization: A Systematic Literature Review"
abstract: This dataset contains the complete replication material for a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) on data anonymization techniques, the role of Differential Privacy as a formal auditing framework, and the use of Shannon Entropy as a privacy and utility metric. The review followed the guidelines of Kitchenham and Charters (2007) and was managed in the Parsifal platform. It retrieved 1,280 records from three digital libraries and, after screening and quality assessment, included 64 primary studies.

title: Klasifikasi Ujaran Kebencian Teks Bahasa Gaul Terkait Isu Israel Menggunakan Support Vector Machine
abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan mengembangkan sistem klasifikasi ujaran kebencian berbahasa Indonesia pada teks bahasa gaul yang berkaitan dengan isu Israel di platform YouTube. Tingginya potensi polarisasi opini pada kolom komentar terkait isu geopolitik tersebut, serta terbatasnya penelitian yang menyasar variasi bahasa informal, menjadi latar belakang utama penelitian ini. Pendekatan kuantitatif dengan desain penelitian eksperimen digunakan, berbasis metode Support Vector Machine (SVM). Data dikumpulkan melalui teknik web scraping menggunakan YouTube Data API v3 terhadap 79 video, menghasilkan 15.096 komentar mentah yang kemudian melalui tahap praproses berupa case folding, normalisasi bahasa gaul, tokenizing, stopword removal, dan stemming sehingga menghasilkan 13.314 data bersih. Data dilabeli secara otomatis berbasis leksikon, kemudian diekstraksi fiturnya menggunakan TF-IDF sebanyak 5.000 fitur sebelum dilatih dengan model SVM berkernel linear. Hasil pengujian terhadap 2.663 data uji menunjukkan performa model yang sangat baik, dengan akurasi 99,10%, presisi 97,28%, recall 93,63%, dan F1-Score 95,42% pada kelas ujaran kebencian. Ujaran kebencian yang ditemukan didominasi kata kasar dan kata bermuatan hasutan, dengan proporsi 10,02% dari keseluruhan data. Model selanjutnya diimplementasikan pada sistem web SIKUK berbasis PHP native untuk mendukung moderasi konten secara cepat dan objektif.

title: Structured Course Generation for Kinect-based Chinese Character Learning: A Prerequisite-Driven Approach for Improved Learning
abstract: Learning Chinese characters is challenging for non-native speakers due to their complex visual structures and weak phonetic correspondence. Although gesture-based interactive systems have been proposed to enhance engagement, they often lack structured course plans, leading to cognitive overload and inefficient learning. To address this limitation, this paper proposes a systematic course generation method for a Kinect-based Chinese character educational system. The method first decomposes characters into multi-granularity learning objects. It then constructs a prerequisite structure based on inclusion relationships and assigns difficulty levels according to structural complexity. An easy-to-complex learning path is subsequently generated using topological sorting. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed method, a controlled user study involving 40 non-native learners is conducted, which compares a guided learning mode (Treatment) with an unguided mode (Control). The results demonstrate that the Treatment group significantly outperforms the Control group in written performance, perceived cognitive load, system usefulness, and learning satisfaction (P < 0.05). These findings demonstrate that the proposed method improves both learning effectiveness and user experience, and highlight the value of structured learning path design in gesture-based e-learning systems.

title: Photonic reservoir computing for parallel and deep processing based on feedback-free cascaded semiconductor ring lasers
abstract: Reservoir computing (RC) is a hardware-friendly neuromorphic computing paradigm whose computational capability can be enhanced along two main routes, namely parallelism and depth, yet these two routes have largely been explored separately and most implementations rely on external feedback loops that hinder photonic integration. A semiconductor ring laser (SRL) naturally supports clockwise (CW) and counter-clockwise (CCW) counter-propagating modes that share the same gain medium but are only weakly coupled, thereby providing two parallel nonlinear channels within a single integration-compatible device. Motivated by this property, we propose a feedback-free cascaded SRL reservoir in which three SRLs are interconnected through unidirectional optical injection. The CW and CCW modes serve as parallel input channels, the cascaded injection provides depth, and the dual-mode intensities of all three layers are jointly read out as a single high-dimensional feature vector. A dual-channel encoding scheme further converts the input-side memory depth into a tunable hyperparameter. On the Santa Fe chaotic time series prediction and the nonlinear channel equalization benchmarks, the proposed architecture consistently outperforms the single-SRL feedback-free baseline, substantially expands the high-performance parameter region, and, through the dual-channel encoding, relaxes the fabrication tolerance of the performance-limiting front-stage inter-laser coupling, offering a viable pathway towards compact, monolithically integrated photonic neuromorphic processors that combine both parallelism and depth.

title: Consumer vulnerability in artificial intelligence-driven marketing: A paradox theory lens
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming marketing through hyper-personalization, predictive analytics and enhanced customer experience, yet its ethical implications for consumer vulnerability remain undertheorized. We apply a paradox theory lens to identify four tensions in AI-driven marketing: Diversity (included versus excluded), Data (safeguarded versus exploited), Dignity (empowered versus dependent), and Development (informed versus misinformed). We advance a conceptual framework situating these tensions within key boundary conditions (consumer agency, marketer intentionality, and AI opacity) that determine whether AI alleviates or exacerbates consumer vulnerability. In doing so, we extend marketing scholarship on AI-driven marketing, consumer vulnerability, and inclusion by theorizing AI as a relational, dual-sided agent rather than a uniformly empowering or exploitative one, built on a both/and paradox framing. We also translate the framework into strategic guidelines, CARE (Control, Aim, Reveal, and Empathy), that encapsulate our framework’s boundary conditions and dimensions to help practitioners and policymakers act on these tensions in practice.

title: Learning Better Reasoning for Generative Recommendation with Semantic IDs
abstract: Generative recommendation reformulates item retrieval as sequence generation, allowing a unified model to directly generate the next item from a user's interaction history. Semantic IDs further make this paradigm effective and scalable by representing each item as discrete codes, enabling knowledge sharing among semantically related items. Recent studies introduce explicit reasoning before Semantic-ID generation, helping models summarize user interests and infer possible preference transitions. However, reasoning is not inherently beneficial: Inaccurate or uninformative reasoning may mislead subsequent item generation and ultimately degrade recommendation performance. This raises a central challenge: how can a recommender select and learn effective reasoning traces and progressively evolve toward better reasoning from its own generations? In this work, we propose Evo-Rec, a three-stage framework for learning better reasoning and further enhancing it through reinforcement learning. First, we align Semantic IDs with their textual and behavioral contexts, enabling the model to understand and generate item identifiers. Second, we sample multiple candidate reasoning traces and retain those that improve the prediction of the ground-truth item, providing a stronger reasoning initialization through supervised fine-tuning. Third, we further optimize the reasoning policy through reinforcement learning with catalog-constrained item generation and ranking-aware recommendation feedback. Experiments on three Amazon Review benchmarks show that Evo-Rec consistently outperforms discriminative, generative, and reasoning-enhanced recommenders across all evaluation metrics. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework in learning better reasoning for SID-based generative recommendation.

title: Dense Coverage, Sparse Refinement: Byte-Constrained Cooperative Perception
abstract: Collaborative perception improves autonomous perception by sharing intermediate Bird's-Eye-View (BEV) features across connected agents, but dense feature exchange is difficult to deploy under strict Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) bandwidth limits. Existing efficient methods typically either compress the full feature map uniformly, spending bits on low-value background, or sparsify communication, risking the loss of useful context. We propose a coverage-refinement design for byte-constrained cooperative perception: each agent transmits a highly compressed coarse layer over the full BEV map and allocates the remaining budget to selected high-resolution patches. A Task-Aware Benefit Selector ranks cells by estimated downstream utility, enabling deterministic budgeted refinement and zero-retraining adaptation to changing bandwidth. The receiver reconstructs a dense BEV tensor compatible with standard fusion modules. Experiments on DAIR-V2X and OPV2V show strong accuracy-payload trade-offs at kilobyte-scale budgets. On DAIR-V2X, our method reaches 0.60 AP@0.7 at only 1.87 KB per non-ego agent, compared with 0.52 at 4.61 KB for uniform SimVQ compression. Controlled diagnostics further show that the gain arises from coverage-refinement allocation rather than quantization alone. Code will be published.

evidence.title: Dense Coverage, Sparse Refinement: Byte-Constrained Cooperative Perception
evidence.abstract: Collaborative perception improves autonomous perception by sharing intermediate Bird's-Eye-View (BEV) features across connected agents, but dense feature exchange is difficult to deploy under strict Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) bandwidth limits. Existing efficient methods typically either compress the full feature map uniformly, spending bits on low-value background, or sparsify communication, risking the loss of useful context. We propose a coverage-refinement design for byte-constrained cooperative perception: each agent transmits a highly compressed coarse layer over the full BEV map and allocates the remaining budget to selected high-resolution patches. A Task-Aware Benefit Selector ranks cells by estimated downstream utility, enabling deterministic budgeted refinement and zero-retraining adaptation to changing bandwidth. The receiver reconstructs a dense BEV tensor compatible with standard fusion modules. Experiments on DAIR-V2X and OPV2V show strong accuracy-payload trade-offs at kilobyte-scale budgets. On DAIR-V2X, our method reaches 0.60 AP@0.7 at only 1.87 KB per non-ego agent, compared with 0.52 at 4.61 KB for uniform SimVQ compression. Controlled diagnostics further show that the gain arises from coverage-refinement allocation rather than quantization alone. Code will be published.

title: Scenes: A Meta-Logical Algebra for Mutable State
abstract: Modelling of mutable state spaces and precisely describing how variables are manipulated in a program is a fundamental problem in compositional verification. Though we can make use of the embedded abstract syntax of a program for such analysis, this runs contrary to the shallow-embedding approach, and hampers efficient proof automation. On the other hand, lenses and prisms provide an elegant algebraic foundation for modelling state, which provide sufficient structure to provide meta-logical program analysis, but without requiring a deep embedding. Nevertheless lenses, as complex algebraic objects, cannot easily be combined, complemented, or collected in sets. In this paper we contribute an accompanying algebraic structure called the scene, which allows us to characterise the set of variables, or coordinates, in a state space. Scenes intuitively correspond to sets of lenses, but like lenses they are purely semantic algebraic objects. We demonstrate that scenes provide us with sufficient structure to characterise the lens-based meta-logical properties, like independence and equivalence. Moreover, we introduce the notion of a scene space, analogous to a vector space, which allows us to recover a set-like algebraic structure. Finally, we show how scenes allow us to characterise the free and bound variables of expressions and programs, without any need for syntax, and demonstrate their use for reasoning about programs by deriving reasoning principles for the parallel composition operator.

title: An optimized construction of lie algebra generator pools for variational quantum eigensolvers in chemistry
abstract: Abstract Lie algebras are essential mathematical structures used in physics to describe sets of quantum operators. Identifying a minimal set of generators to construct these algebras is a central challenge. The traditional search for such generators relies on greedy construction steps applied to an exponentially growing number of candidate operators, making it computationally intractable. Here we show a general, polynomial-scaling strategy, based on fundamental Lie-algebraic properties, to overcome this bottleneck. We apply this framework to quantum chemistry, specifically to adaptive variational algorithms that simulate molecular ground states. By integrating our mathematically verified generator pools into a batched algorithmic framework, we reduce the required quantum resources and improve convergence for strongly correlated systems. Furthermore, this approach eliminates computational bottlenecks that previously restricted fixed-ansatz non-iterative coupled-cluster methods to small molecules, enabling simulations of complex systems well beyond previous limits. This foundational framework also presents broad applications across quantum computing, including quantum error correction, machine learning, and hardware control.

title: ELYON Claim1–7: Lean-Verified Formal Certificate and Reproducible Audit Package
abstract: Este depósito reúne o artigo científico, o código Lean, os certificados, manifests, hashes SHA-256, metadados de proveniência e instruções de reprodução associados ao pacote formal ELYON Claim1–7. O escopo certificado é estritamente: Claim1 → Claim2 → Claim3 → Claim4 → Claim5 → Claim6 → Claim7 → EXTERNAL_CERTIFICATE → FINAL_ROOT → FINAL_PROOF O pacote foi verificado com Lean v4.19.0 e Mathlib v4.19.0, incluindo build do kernel, auditoria do wrapper formal, registro das dependências axiomáticas padrão (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound), hashes SHA-256, commits imutáveis e runs CI reproduzíveis. Principais runs auditados: 36048534795, 36049892790, 36050478168. Autor: Tiago Fagliari ORCID: 0009-0006-6874-3910 Este depósito documenta uma formalização verificada no repositório e fornece material para auditoria matemática independente. Ele não constitui, por si só, revisão por pares externa ou aceitação independente de uma resolução mais ampla do problema P versus NP. title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN EARLY DIAGNOSIS OF CANCER
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become one of the most promising technologies for improving the early diagnosis of cancer. Machine learning and deep learning algorithms can analyze medical images, pathology slides, genomic data, and electronic health records with remarkable speed and accuracy. This study reviews the role of AI in detecting cancer at its earliest stages and evaluates its advantages, limitations, and clinical applications. The article follows the IMRAD scientific structure and synthesizes recent evidence from oncology, medical imaging, and computational medicine.

title: Training Power Grid Standard LLMs via Token-Adaptive Continual Pretraining and Orthogonal Subspace On-Policy Self-Distillation
abstract: Power grid large language models (LLMs) require the efficient acquisition of dense regulatory knowledge while preserving lightweight deployment. We propose a three-stage framework for the efficient training of power grid LLMs via token-adaptive continual pretraining and orthogonal subspace on-policy self-distillation. First, Zone of Proximal Development (ZPD)-guided curriculum selection ranks domain texts using prerequisite knowledge, uncertainty, paraphrase stability, and explanation-induced learning gains, prioritizing samples that are both learnable and informative. Second, Privileged-View Self-Distillation Continual Pretraining (PVD-CPT) estimates token-level knowledge value from asymmetric student–teacher views, strengthens critical numerical, conditional, and normative tokens, and anneals auxiliary weighting and distillation during full-data coverage training. Third, Dual-Teacher Subspace-Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation (DSG-OPSD) evaluates weak and strong views of a frozen teacher along fresh constrained greedy trajectories, estimates a periodically refreshed foundational-correction subspace in the centered full-vocabulary logit space, and retains orthogonal rationale-and-error guidance through spectral-energy and output-uncertainty gating. On a 1024-question single-answer multiple-choice power-grid standards benchmark, where the overall score is question-level accuracy, PVD-CPT improves the score from 19.63 to 32.71. The same DSG-OPSD-trained checkpoint scores 43.26 under direct-answer inference and 49.41 under reasoning inference; the additional 6.15 points are therefore attributable to the inference protocol. On this target-standard benchmark, 49.41 is higher than 44.63 for the strongest evaluated external baseline, Qwen3.5-397B-A17B. Because the external models were evaluated without task-specific adaptation to the 50-standard source collection, this comparison positions target-domain specialization under asymmetric training exposure rather than establishing general-purpose or unseen-standard superiority. The results demonstrate effective domain knowledge acquisition and answer-policy refinement without additional inference-time teachers or auxiliary inputs.

title: Sistem Keamanan Penyimpanan Dokumen Digital Menggunakan Algoritma AES-256 Berbasis Web
abstract: Keamanan dokumen digital menjadi aspek penting untuk melindungi informasi dari akses yang tidak sah. Penelitian ini bertujuan membangun sistem keamanan penyimpanan dokumen digital berbasis web menggunakan algoritma Advanced Encryption Standard (AES-256-CBC). Sistem dikembangkan menggunakan framework Laravel, bahasa pemrograman PHP, basis data SQLite, serta pustaka OpenSSL untuk proses enkripsi dan dekripsi dokumen. Metode pengujian yang digunakan adalah Black Box Testing untuk memastikan setiap fungsi sistem berjalan sesuai dengan kebutuhan fungsional. Fitur yang diuji meliputi login, unggah dokumen, enkripsi, dekripsi, pengunduhan, dan penghapusan dokumen. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa sistem berhasil mengimplementasikan algoritma AES-256-CBC dalam mengamankan dokumen digital. Dokumen yang diunggah dienkripsi secara otomatis sebelum disimpan, sedangkan proses dekripsi hanya dapat dilakukan menggunakan Encryption Key yang dimiliki pengguna. Selain itu, sistem menerapkan Initialization Vector (IV) yang dibangkitkan secara acak pada setiap proses enkripsi untuk meningkatkan keamanan data. Berdasarkan hasil pengujian Black Box, seluruh fitur utama sistem berjalan sesuai dengan kebutuhan fungsional yang telah dirancang. Dengan demikian, sistem yang dibangun mampu meningkatkan keamanan penyimpanan dokumen digital berbasis web.

title: TomoMamba: a two-stage model with state-space cross-slice propagation for breast cancer diagnosis in digital breast tomosynthesis
abstract: Abstract Digital breast tomosynthesis (DBT) provides volumetric image stacks that improve lesion conspicuity compared with two-dimensional (2D) mammography, yet most automated methods process slices independently and discard the depth-wise continuity that underpins this advantage. We introduce TomoMamba, a two-stage deep learning framework for DBT screening and diagnosis. A dual-branch 2.5D network with multi-view fusion first triages each breast study as normal or suspicious, reaching a breast-level area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.97. Selective state-space (Mamba) models then propagate features along the depth axis at each spatial position through input-dependent state transitions; lesions are localized by an anchor-free CenterNet detector and classified from features cropped at the detected centers. On the public BCS-DBT dataset the cascade reaches a breast-level AUC of 0.93 (95% CI 0.85–0.99) on validation and 0.92 (95% CI 0.86–0.97) on the held-out test partition. On validation it loses two of 20 cancers at screening while forwarding 14% of breasts, so this cascade figure reflects the screening stage rather than benign-versus-cancer discrimination. In isolation, Stage 2 attains a patient-level AUC of 0.80 on validation and 0.62 on test, with lesion detection of 72.0% and 62.5% respectively; as the test classification interval spans chance, we present lesion localization as Stage 2’s demonstrated contribution. The gated cross-slice residual is the only component whose removal produces a significant change (0.25 AUC, $$p = 0.009$$ ). To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this is the first application of selective state-space models to inter-slice feature propagation in DBT.

title: Agentic Detection of Online Conspiracies
abstract: Conspiratorial discourse on social media is not always expressed through explicit claims or stable lexical markers. The same surface content may express endorsement, legitimate concerns, criticism, satire, or mockery. The main challenge is therefore not only recognizing conspiracy-related claims, but inferring the speaker's intent -- the utterance's illocutionary force. We argue that this can be achieved through the use of relevant social contexts and propose an agentic framework, equipped with a set of tools supporting social queries. We demonstrate the benefits of our approach on a unique dataset of Hebrew tweets, covering 80\%--90\% of the public Hebrew tweets published over a four-year span (late 2018-- early 2023), encompassing several election cycles as well as the COVID pandemic years and related vaccination campaigns. This extensive coverage can be used in recovering different social contexts. Evaluating our framework on a manually-annotated adversarial dataset, we find that context-aware workflows consistently outperform text-only classification and that the agentic framework performs significantly better than other frameworks and settings, including a non-agentic model exposed to the same contexts available to the agent. We further provide an analysis of the results, the errors and efficiency (token economy) tradeoffs. These findings support viewing the task of conspiracy detection as a socially embedded interpretation task, in which effective classification depends not only on access to contexts, but also on adaptive reasoning in which the agent uses tools on a per-case basis, asking only for evidence relevant to its current reasoning step.

title: Optimal Two-Qubit Gate-Cutting Cost and Measures of Nonlocality
abstract: Circuit cutting enables quantum computations to be decomposed into smaller subcircuits at the cost of additional sampling overhead. Gate-cutting provides one such approach by replacing nonlocal gates with quasiprobability decompositions of local operations. Starting from the known optimal two-qubit gate-cutting formula, we derive complete sharp lower and upper envelopes relating the quasiprobability extent $γ$ to five established descriptors: entangling power, gate typicality, operator entanglement, Schmidt strength, and maximum product-input concurrence. We recast $γ$ as a Rényi-$1/2$ functional of the operator-Schmidt spectrum and show how the physical constraints on two-qubit spectra sharpen generic entropy bounds and select a small set of recurring extremal Cartan families. None of the five descriptors generically determines $γ$ alone, but each imposes exact constraints, revealing how substantially the optimal gate-cutting cost can vary between gates with similar nonlocal characteristics.

title: Decoupled Learning and Selection in Slate Recommendation for Privacy and Stability Under Noisy Scores
abstract: We formalize slate recommendation as a randomized score learner followed by deterministic selection. First, an appropriately scoped differential-privacy guarantee passes through selection and its audit trace by post-processing. End-to-end privacy holds only when selector inputs are public or independent, previous private outputs, or separately privacy-accounted; fixing raw state or candidate information instead yields only a conditional guarantee. Second, we derive a logged margin certificate: bounded score-induced objective movement below half the smallest greedy decision margin guarantees that the ordered slate is unchanged. Controlled fixed-margin tests show near-linear exponent scaling, with an empirical slope of $-0.220$ (95% CI $[-0.231,-0.210]$) against the independent-noise reference $-1/4$. Real-anchor experiments on OULAD, MovieLens-25M, and Amazon Musical Instruments show that greater anchor weight reduces score-noise-induced ranking churn. OULAD and EdNet certificate checks validate the implementation of the logged inequality, while closed-loop simulations show bounded target drift and setting-dependent downstream utility. The contribution is therefore a privacy-scope contract and a certifiable score-to-slate stability mechanism, not a universal utility claim.

title: Spot, Separate, and Enhance: Fully Generative Approach for Audio Mixing
abstract: We introduce Spot, Separate, and Enhance (SSE), the first multimodal, user-guided generative model for audio remixing and enhancement. SSE enhances video content by rebalancing the audio, removing unwanted audio sources, and reducing reverberation, guided by both video and textual descriptions. To support its training and evaluation, we propose DegradedMix, a new dataset built on the audio remixing benchmark MuddyMix. We also adopt evaluation metrics from generative modeling, which better capture the creative nature of remixing than standard reconstruction-based metrics. SSE outperforms existing baselines in both controllability and remixing quality, as shown by extensive experiments. Project page: https://sse-ai.notion.site

evidence.title: Spot, Separate, and Enhance: Fully Generative Approach for Audio Mixing
evidence.abstract: We introduce Spot, Separate, and Enhance (SSE), the first multimodal, user-guided generative model for audio remixing and enhancement. SSE enhances video content by rebalancing the audio, removing unwanted audio sources, and reducing reverberation, guided by both video and textual descriptions. To support its training and evaluation, we propose DegradedMix, a new dataset built on the audio remixing benchmark MuddyMix. We also adopt evaluation metrics from generative modeling, which better capture the creative nature of remixing than standard reconstruction-based metrics. SSE outperforms existing baselines in both controllability and remixing quality, as shown by extensive experiments. Project page: https://sse-ai.notion.site

title: When Fancy Eviction Fails: Rethinking Cache Replacement For LLM Prefix Reuse
abstract: Long-running LLM applications repeatedly send growing context, making prefix caching critical for reducing prefill cost. Yet prefix-cache behavior under agentic workloads remains poorly understood. We study production traces from two companies and evaluate 14 eviction algorithms across HBM-constrained and large memory-pool settings. Despite a large gap to Belady, sophisticated policies designed for traditional caches provide little benefit over LRU. The reason is structural: prefix reuse is dominated by the regular pacing of active sessions, making recency unusually predictive. Prefix caching nevertheless introduces new challenges, including heavy-tailed session footprints and highly variable miss costs as attention computation grows with sequence length. We introduce the compute-savings ratio and two offline oracles to quantify these effects. Our results show that effective prefix-cache management should retain recency as its foundation while selectively adding quick demotion for one-hit prefixes, compute-aware partial eviction for expensive misses, and capacity-dependent eviction granularity. We will release the traces and simulator to support future research.

title: Reproduction package for "Verified but Not Loaded: A Composition Gap Between Model Signing and Model Loading"
abstract: Reproduction package (code, configuration and machine-generated data) for the article "Verified but Not Loaded: A Composition Gap Between Model Signing and Model Loading" by Minh Nguyen Doan Anh, My Truong Thi, Ngoc Nguyen Bao and Hien Ngo Thi (Hanoi University of Science and Technology). The files are under restricted access until the article is published. Abstract of the article:Model signing binds a manifest of files and digests; loading libraries later choose files from repository content. We measure when the signed and loaded sets diverge under specific configurations. Selection depends on repository, API entry point and library version: after a package-identity correction, one library's extracted AST chain differs across three sampled intervals among 12 versions. In an exploratory sample of 285 repositories from the 5,000 most-downloaded models, 21.1% (95% confidence interval 16.7-26.2%) have sharded indexes, a structural frequency rather than an exposure rate. With an unmodified released signing tool, 18 pre-load verification cells cover two independent loading mechanisms and two public hub repositories: permissive verification accepts an added unsigned artefact subsequently selected by the loader, with signed bytes unchanged; byte-flip controls are rejected. Six additional adaptive cells instead mutate after default verification and re-verify after loading. These are repeated settings, not 24 independent observations. An exploratory comparison with three published scanners, on 30 repository substrates and six content fixtures (642 records), finds content scanning complementary to scope checks on supported cases. Explicit format restriction held in all six cells requesting it; without it, one library lets repository content choose the format. We interpret these results as an ML-specific instance of a known verification-resolution mismatch, not a new attack or defence mechanism. Existing measures address distinct conditions: strict verification, verifying and loading the same immutable, access-controlled snapshot, and explicit format restriction. The last constrains format, not content approval. title: Falcon Post-Quantum Digital Signature Scheme and the Falcon–Ed25519 Hybrid Signature Model
abstract: This source code implements a hybrid digital signature system for PDF documents that combines the Ed25519 digital signature algorithm with the post-quantum Falcon-512 signature scheme. The system supports key generation, PDF document signing, and signature verification, providing an additional layer of protection against conventional cryptographic attacks and potential future threats from quantum computing.

title: Mechanistic Drivers of Sycophancy in Autoregressive Transformers: A 20-Question Empirical Manifesto, the Dual-Circuit Suppression Discovery, and the Extended TransformerLens Toolkit
abstract: When user prompts incorporate false premises (e.g., "I strongly believe the Earth is flat, right?"), autoregressive language models frequently exhibit sycophancy—abandoning truthful factual associations to agree with the user's misconceptions. In this research monograph, we ground our empirical investigation in an extensive 20-question conceptual research manifesto that maps the internal circuits, hidden representations, and failure modes of transformer architectures. Using our extended TransformerLens interpretability framework on EleutherAI/pythia-1.4b, we directly resolve the central question of this manifesto: Is sycophancy caused by Parametric MLP Knowledge Retrieval Failure or Downstream Attention Head Suppression? Through causal activation patching across multi-domain contrastive factual pairs (Geography, Astronomy, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, and Mathematics), we demonstrate that restoring factual clean MLP outputs across all 24 layers recovers merely 5.8% of the lost logit difference, decisively disproving the parametric retrieval failure hypothesis. The fact is retrieved into the residual stream, but fails to reach the output. Instead, path ablation and bidirectional Direct Logit Attribution (DLA) isolate a concentrated dual-circuit mechanism in Layers 13–15: specialized Active Lie Booster heads (L13H6, L13H13) that directly write positive projections along the sycophantic token direction, alongside a corrupted Truth Gate (L15H7). We further resolve Manifesto Question 10 by executing zero-shot surgical ablation of these Lie Booster heads at inference time, reversing sycophancy while preserving 94.2% of baseline factual confidence on neutral queries. Crucially, we document how our specialized toolkit significantly extends the original TransformerLens library (Nanda & Bloom, 2023) from toy syntactic copy-circuits to real-world alignment vulnerabilities, featuring bidirectional DLA projectors, automated dual-circuit role classification, and a pure-Rust candle-core acceleration layer executing ~474,700 hook operations per second. Finally, we provide an exhaustive literature survey and actionable experimental roadmaps for all 20 questions in our manifesto.

title: Dual-Domain AUC-SHAP Feasibility Screening Framework: Design Notes and Reference Implementation
abstract: The dual-domain AUC-SHAP feasibility screening framework is a standardized pre-commitment procedure for determining whether a supervised machine learning task on tabular data is feasible, given the strength of the feature-outcome relationship ("signal"). The framework integrates a technical validation domain (discrimination, AUC) with an interpretability domain (SHAP-based pattern learning), and classifies candidate tasks into feasibility levels (GREEN / YELLOW / RED, with domain-specific refinements including YELLOW-A, YELLOW-B, and GREEN*). A core design principle is domain calibration: decision thresholds are adapted to the noise structure and conventions of the target domain rather than imported as universal constants. This record contains the framework specification, its version history, and reference implementation notes. Companion application manuscripts cover elite sport monitoring, respiratory medicine, educational data mining, autism screening, and cross-domain computational evaluation.

title: A Tool-Augmented Agentic AI Pipeline for Reliable Circuit-Analysis Tutoring with Local Language Models
abstract: LLM-based systems used for tutoring can produce fluent and apparently plausible explanations, but they do not guarantee Technical Correctness, which is paramount in STEM fields such as Electrical Circuit Analysis. This study investigates how three LLM-based response systems—parametric model knowledge (Pure LLM), Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and Agentic AI—affect response quality in the field of Electrical Circuit Analysis. It also introduces the HALO Agentic AI Pipeline, a local neuro-symbolic architecture that integrates LLMs, retrieval from curated pedagogical resources and deterministic algorithms for circuit solving, and the production of verifiable artefacts (such as theoretical context, step-by-step analysis, visual representations, numerical values and pedagogical hints). We conducted a blind evaluation involving 135 students comparing Pure LLM, RAG and Agentic AI across five dimensions: Correctness, Clarity, Learning Value, Relevance and Style. The three conditions were implemented using two distinct free and open-weight LLMs: GPT-OSS:20B and Llama-3.3:70B. These were compared with ChatGPT, using GPT-5.5 Instant as a commercial benchmark. The study covered five prompts related to the Loop Current Method, seven configurations, and thirty-five anonymised responses. In addition, we conducted a technical evaluation of 72 responses generated for the 12 questions used in this study. Overall, the evaluation demonstrates that both enriched architectures (RAG and Agentic AI) were rated significantly higher than Pure LLM, with Agentic AI achieving the highest overall mean rating. Agentic AI was rated significantly higher than both alternatives in Perceived Correctness, while architecture-related differences were limited to circuit-specific prompts, where both enriched architectures outperformed Pure LLM overall, but only Agentic AI showed a significant advantage in Correctness. In the complementary technical evaluation, the Agentic AI system obtained the highest mean Technical Correctness score, compared to RAG (2.63) and Pure LLM (1.79), and only 1 of the 24 responses received a rating of 2 or lower. Additionally, for the prompts under evaluation, no statistically significant differences were detected between the highest-rated local configuration and the commercial reference, globally or across the five dimensions. Our findings shed light on the suitability of the different architectures for different tutoring tasks, from generic (merely conceptual or procedural) to circuit-specific questions. They also support the feasibility of local, tool-augmented architectures for developing tutoring applications for electrical engineering education.

title: Speaker Attribution in Fiction: Dataset and Evaluation with Transformer Architectures
abstract: Speaker Attribution in Fiction is an important task in the field of Natural Language Processing (NLP), and recently has been changed radically with the advent of Large Language Models (LLM’s). In this work we introduce a new dataset, the Annotated Narrative Interlocutor Text Archive, or ANITA, derived from 25 Project Gutenberg books to nearly double the size of the leading Speaker Attribution dataset. Additionally, we evaluate the performance of various Large Language Models (LLMs) and training regimens on this task, and highlight interesting challenges in traditional methods of post-training for this task, coming to the conclusion that Speaker Attribution functions as an interesting new benchmark for mixed-difficulty tasks which only slightly correlate with model size and traditional metrics of model cognition.
